components.evidence: Both arms and hands are continuous with one athlete in the original frame.
The extended left hand visibly wraps the dark central grip within the white riser.
Black finger protection covers the exact string-hook boundary; proximity to the diagonal string does not establish each hooking contact.
The drawing hand is near the lower face, but a direct underside-jaw anchor surface is not exposed; facial adjacency is not that contact.
One horizontal arrow crosses the bow window above the gripping hand, but its actual receiving rest interface is partly hidden by the riser. Alignment alone does not prove the support contact.

An orange rear connector lies beside the drawing fingers where the string passes, but its direct latch/seat to the same string is too overlapped to confirm at original native scale. The white fletching is visible and is not used as a substitute for the latch.
Lower recurve tip is visible near the athlete's lower torso level; upper limb leaves the top border and upper tip is absent.
Lower segment is traceable to the visible lower tip, while upper segment runs beyond the top border. The complete three-endpoint mechanism is unavailable in one image.
Both soles visibly meet the grass and remain fully inside the original frame.
A circular colored target on a straw backstop is visible downrange toward the direction of the arrow; the generated placement is screen right rather than the optional screen-left staging.

testcase_gates.evidence: A single athlete holds a recurve-style bow under draw with arrow, forearm protection, practice line and visible target. This supports a sport-practice scene, not a score, victory or verified rule compliance.

The face retains the supplied image's softly rounded contours, large dark eyes and natural pink lips at the available scale; a dark chin-length bob and fine parted bangs are directly visible. This is visible appearance correspondence, not identity, age, personality or consent verification.
The central grip and same-actor ownership pass; the exact drawing-finger hook, underside-jaw anchor and nock-string latch remain partly occluded. Composite gate fails when any endpoint is partial.
Upper bow tip and the complete upper string route are outside the saved image; the lower segment and grip cannot replace the missing full route.
Both shoe-ground supports pass, while the required simultaneous full-bow endpoint visibility fails because the top limb is cropped.

limits: Exact draw-hand contacts overlap at the chosen projection
